minutes.headline: Board voted not to support the new HR director position without more evidence, over objections it lacked a full board.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard the town manager's FY20 preliminary budget highlights, with sharp disagreement over a proposed part-time HR director/assistant town manager and a seasonal parks director. A motion not to support the HR position was put to a vote despite objections that the board was short a member. The board also reviewed the draft May 4 town meeting warrant, approved the Arts Festival, a solar pilot warrant article and a cultural council appointment, then went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Announced the pancake breakfast at the Eagle House the next morning.
Read a letter from a resident asking that two citizens join the task force studying alternatives to replacing the gas and diesel tanks.
Red Sox World Series trophy visiting the Eagle House April 7 as a fundraiser.
Asked that important articles be moved earlier if town meeting runs two days, and preferred consecutive Saturdays.
Said the earlier vote on the HR position disregarded open meeting law because the agenda did not say a vote may be taken.
Supported the town manager's staffing recommendations given the town's growth.
Wanted town meeting to run straight through with no lunch break.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted not to support a new HR director/assistant town manager position without more evidence it cannot be done by other means; the vote outcome was not audible.
The town manager is to bring more information on the HR and recreation positions to the next meeting.
The board heard FY20 preliminary budget highlights, including target-budget staffing requests and school, Monty Tech and health insurance assumptions.
The board voted to put a BGO Solar pilot warrant article on the May town meeting warrant.
Warrant articles on building sales and the TCP design were deferred until the full board is present next week.

why_it_matters: New town positions and the school and health insurance assumptions feed the FY20 budget, which sets what the town budget, mostly taxes, asks of residents at the May 4 town meeting.
A resident at public comment said the HR vote broke the open meeting law because the agenda did not say a vote might be taken, so the position may be taken up again.
watch_next: Next week's meeting: the town manager's added information on the HR and recreation positions, and the deferred building sales and TCP design warrant articles.
